Subject: Ephemeral IPs and outbound egress for Redwood private connector

Hi Markus,

We're working through final network signoff for the private connector deployment into our prod VPC next month. Two items came up from our security team that I need your help clarifying so we can open the firewall change ticket:

1) Ephemeral source addresses: our current infra team wants to know if Redwood's private endpoint ever originates traffic from ephemeral IPs that would rotate per instance (makes allowlisting impossible). We prefer a small static pool to add to our perimeter allowlist.
2) Outbound ports and DNS: we need a concise list of outbound ports and hostnames (or SNI) that must be allowed, and whether Redwood expects TLS inspection or will require SNI-based allowlisting only.

Attached is our draft egress policy matrix (acme-egress-policy.xlsx) and the manifest you asked for. Can you confirm the expected egress behavior and propose a recommended allowlist approach?

Thanks,
James

Senior Cloud Architect, Acme Health
From: markus_klein@redwood.example

Cc: dev_patel@redwood.example, laura_bennett@redwood.example, monica_patel@redwood.example
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 13:04:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral IPs and outbound egress for Redwood private connector

James — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Quick summary up front: we can avoid ephemeral source IPs for customer-facing private connectors by routing outbound control-plane/service calls through one of two patterns; both are compatible with strict allowlists:

Option A (customer-managed NAT): All outbound calls originate from your NAT/egress gateway. We provide DNAT-friendly routing and the connector runs in your VPC. You manage the static egress IP(s) and add them to your perimeter. Recommended when customers require full control over egress and observability.

Option B (Redwood-managed egress bridge): We provision a small, customer-dedicated outbound proxy in your region (our infra) that uses a stable AWS/GCP static pool we own; you allowlist our advertised pool. This reduces ops for you but requires an allowlist entry for our pool.

Details and caveats: 
- Ephemeral IPs: the connector itself can run on ephemeral host IPs, but control-plane and model download traffic can be pinned to the NAT/proxy path above so source IPs seen by your firewall will be stable.
- Ports/hosts: primary traffic is HTTPS (443) to our control plane (*.redwood-inference.net) and model artifact storage (s3/gcs endpoints we list). We do not require TLS interception; SNI/domain allowlist is sufficient.
- DNS: If you use DNS-based allowlists, ensure resolution from your egress path (NAT/proxy) returns expected A records. If your DNS uses split-horizon, coordinate so the egress device resolves against your resolver.
- Failover: if the dedicated proxy loses connectivity, the connector can fallback to a secondary path; if you need strict egress prevention, enable strict policy in the manifest (we'll document how).

I'll have Dev add the exact service FQDNs and the minimal port list. For now, recommend opening 443 outbound for TLS and 53 if you require recursive DNS from the connector.

Next steps: Dev, can you enumerate the FQDNs, static IP block (if Redwood-managed) and any required DNS entries? James — if you prefer Option A, confirm the NAT CIDR you'll use and we'll validate routing in our pre-prod test.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.example

Subject: Re: Ephemeral IPs and outbound egress for Redwood private connector

Following up with the specifics Markus promised. Below are the pieces you can paste into your firewall ticket. I kept the list minimal to reduce ACL churn.

If you choose Option A (customer NAT):
- Required outbound ports from connector instances (egress): TCP 443 (control plane + model pulls), TCP 123 (optional NTP if you enforce time checks), UDP 53 only if the connector is resolving DNS directly.
- Hostnames to allow (SNI-based allowlist OK): control.redwood-inference.net, artifacts.redwood-inference.net, metrics.redwood-inference.net.
- No TLS interception required; we use certificate pinning for the control channel.

If you choose Option B (Redwood-managed egress):
- Allowlist the following IPv4 blocks (our advertised pool for your region): 35.198.48.128/27, 34.102.176.0/28. We'll announce any rotation 72 hours in advance.
- FQDNs as above still apply for domain-level checks.

Additional operational notes:
- Ephemeral NAT: if you run connector in an autoscaling group behind your NAT, source IPs seen by your firewall are the NAT IPs (stable).
- Short-lived outbound sockets: model downloads are HTTP(S) GETs; we recommend rate limits on your side to avoid transient bursts causing IDS alerts during rollout.
- Audit: we push connection logs to your SIEM via a syslog sink if you enable the telemetry option in the manifest.

I'll attach a PDF change request template for your firewall team and a one-page diagram on the Drive link Markus listed.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
